title: Choice Independence Outside Guessing States
statement: Let $S$ and $V$ be deterministic Turing machines over the binary alphabet, and let $q$ be a state of the reverse host that is not a live scheduler state (a state of the form consisting of a scheduler state paired with an active scheduler phase). For every input symbol, possibly blank, and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the host's transition action is the same for choice bit $0$ as for choice bit $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $S,V$ are finite deterministic machines over the binary alphabet
$q$ is a reverse-host state distinct from every live scheduler state
the input symbol is an optional Boolean symbol
the work-tape symbols are a tuple indexed by the host's work tapes
replaced: Let $S$ and $V$ be deterministic machines and let $q$ be any control state of the reverse host built from $S$ and $V$ that is not a live guessing state. For every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the two transition tables of the host agree at $q$.
